literal: With the world to agree conducting oneself, many things even having learned, unlearned are they without wisdom.
translation: Those who do not know how to conduct themselves in harmony with the world are truly unlearned, even if they have learned many things.
modern: உலகத்தோடு ஒத்து வாழும் முறையை அறியாதவர்கள், பல நூல்களைக் கற்றிருந்தாலும் அறிவில்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
explanation: The word arivu can mean general knowledge or intellect, but here it specifically means the practical wisdom of proper conduct, fitting the chapter on decorum. This couplet defines true wisdom as the ability to live in harmony with the world. The phrase ulakattotu otta ozhukal emphasizes conducting oneself in agreement with the accepted norms of society. Even if a person has acquired vast textual knowledge, denoted by pala karrum, it is useless without this practical social wisdom. Therefore, the author concludes that such people are effectively unlearned.
